item.title: Theoretical framework and key technologies of spatio-temporal intelligence for satellite remote sensing constellations
item.dc:title: Theoretical framework and key technologies of spatio-temporal intelligence for satellite remote sensing constellations
item.dc:creator: Mi Wang Tengteng Dong Jing Xiao Qianyu Wu Deren Li a State Key Laboratory of Information Engineering in Surveying, Mapping and Remote Sensing, Wuhan University, Wuhan, Chinab National Engineering Research Center for Multimedia Software, School of Artificial Intelligence, Wuhan University, Wuhan, ChinaMi Wang received the B.Eng., M.Sc., and Ph.D. degrees in photogrammetry and remote sensing from Wuhan University in 1997, 1999, and 2001, respectively. Since 2008, he has been a Professor with the State Key Laboratory of Information Engineering in Surveying, Mapping and Remote Sensing, Wuhan University. His research interests include measurable seamless stereo ortho-image databases, geographic information systems (GIS), and high-precision remote-sensing image processing and intelligent spatial information service.Tengteng Dong received the B.Eng. degree from the Jilin University in 2022. He is currently pursuing his Ph.D. degree with the State Key Laboratory of Information Engineering in Surveying, Mapping and Remote Sensing, Wuhan University. His research focuses on high-precision processing of multimodal remote sensing images.Jing Xiao received the B.Sc. and M.Sc. degrees in computer science and technology from Wuhan University in 2006 and 2008, respectively, and the Ph.D. degree in computer science and technology from the Institute of Geo-Information Science and Earth Observation, Twente University, in 2013. She was a Project Researcher with the National Institute of Informatics from 2019 to 2020. She is currently a Professor with the National Engineering Research Center for Multimedia Software, School of Artificial Intelligence, Wuhan University. Her research interests include image/video processing and compression and analysis.Qianyu Wu received the B.Sc. degree in Geographic Information Systems from Henan University of Economics and Law in 2016, and the M.Sc. degree in Surveying and Mapping Engineering from the Aerospace Information Research Institute, Chinese Academy of Sciences, in 2019. She obtained her Ph.D. degree in Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing from the State Key Laboratory of Information Engineering in Surveying, Mapping and Remote Sensing, Wuhan University, in 2024. Her research interests include satellite mission planning and real-time intelligent services for remote sensing satellites.Deren Li received the Ph.D. degree from the University of Stuttgart in 1985, and the Honorary Doctorate degree from ETH Zürich in 2008. He was the President of Wuhan Technical University of Surveying and Mapping and later served as the Director of the Academic Committee at Wuhan University, where he was also the Director of the State Key Laboratory of Information Engineering in Surveying, Mapping and Remote Sensing (LIESMARS). He is currently the Honorary Director of the Academic Committee, LIESMARS, the Director of the Collaborative Innovation Center of Geospatial Technology, an Honorary Chairperson of the Wuhan Association for Science and Technology, and the Chief Scientist of the Optics Valley of China in Wuhan. Prof. Li is an Honorary Member and a fellow of the International Society for Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing (ISPRS), a member of the International Eurasia Academy of Sciences and the International Academy of Astronautics, and holds dual memberships of the Chinese Academy of Sciences and the Chinese Academy of Engineering. He won the highest award, the “Brock Gold Medal Award,” from ISPRS in 2022. His research interests include geospatial informatics and spatiotemporal intelligence.

item.title: Polar remote sensing in China: advances, integrated observation systems, and future perspectives
item.dc:title: Polar remote sensing in China: advances, integrated observation systems, and future perspectives
item.dc:creator: Xiao Cheng Ye Peng Chuyue Peng Tian Yang Yibo Li Bangsong Wang a School of Geospatial Engineering and Science, Sun Yat-sen University, Zhuhai, Chinab Southern Marine Science and Engineering Guangdong Laboratory (Zhuhai), Zhuhai, Chinac Key Laboratory of Comprehensive Observation of Polar Environment, Ministry of Education, Sun Yat-sen University, Zhuhai, Chinad Shenzhen Feima Robotics Co., Ltd., Shenzhen, Chinae Tianjin Feima Robotics Technology Co., Ltd., Tianjin, ChinaXiao Cheng received his bachelor’s degree in surveying engineering from Wuhan Technical University of Surveying and Mapping in 1998 and his master’s degree in geodesy from Wuhan University in 2001. He received his Ph.D. in cartography and geographic information systems from the Graduate University of the Chinese Academy of Sciences in 2004. After completing his Ph.D., he joined the Institute of Remote Sensing Applications, Chinese Academy of Sciences. In 2009, he joined Beijing Normal University as a professor and associate dean of the College of Global Change and Earth System Science, becoming dean in 2016. In 2019, he joined Sun Yat-sen University as a professor, helped establish the School of Geospatial Engineering and Science, and served as its dean. He has authored or coauthored more than 200 peer-reviewed papers, including articles in Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences and Remote Sensing of Environment. In 2017, he received the Award for Advanced Individual of China’s Polar Exploration. His research interests include polar remote sensing and polar climate change.Ye Peng received a bachelor’s degree in geographic information science from Beijing Forestry University and is currently pursuing a master’s degree in surveying and mapping science and technology at the School of Geospatial Engineering and Science, Sun Yat-sen University. Her research interests are polar remote sensing and cryospheric change.Chuyue Peng received the Ph.D. degree in cartography and geographic information systems from Sun Yat-sen University. She is currently a postdoctoral researcher at Sun Yat-sen University. She has authored or coauthored 7 publications in refereed journals. Her research interests include snow and firn stratigraphy and ice sheet surface mass balance, with a focus on combining airborne radar observations and deep learning to investigate Antarctic snow accumulation and changes in the cryosphere.Tian Yang received the M.S. degree in resources and environment from the School of Geospatial Engineering and Science, Sun Yat-sen University, where he is currently pursuing the Ph.D. degree in remote sensing science and technology. His research interests include polar remote sensing, Antarctic ice-sheet dynamics, subglacial hydrology, and ice–ocean interactions, with a particular focus on monitoring cryospheric changes using multisource satellite observations, including altimetry, optical imagery, and synthetic aperture radar (SAR).Yibo Li received his bachelor’s degree in Surveying and Mapping Engineering from China University of Mining and Technology in 2023. He is currently pursuing a Ph.D. at the School of Geospatial Engineering and Science, Sun Yat-sen University. His research interests include polar observations using small unmanned aerial and underwater vehicles, sea-ice observation, glacial geomorphology, and cartography.Bangsong Wang is affiliated with Shenzhen Feima Robotics Co., Ltd. and Tianjin Feima Robotics Technology Co.,Ltd.,China. His work includes the development of calibration methods for cameras and LiDAR sensors used in UAV surveying.
